Listen to this article Share …Votes 65% to CAPEX, 35% to OPEX Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State, on Monday, presented the State’s 2027 Appropriation Bill of N1.23 trillion to the State House of Assembly for consideration, debate and approval. He said that the budget proposal was N493.01 billion or 28.5% lower than the N1.729 trillion approved for 2026; a reduction, he said, reflected a deliberate decision to adopt realistic spending projections and strengthen fiscal discipline. In the 2027 budget christened, “Budget of Sustained Prosperity and Enhanced Growth”, the governor proposed to allocate 65% to capital expenditure. Read also: Delta approves over N1.2trn 2027 budget, roads, other projects “The sum of N806.8 billion is proposed for capital expenditure and N430 billion for recurrent expenditure”, he said. He explained that the budget would consolidate ongoing projects, stimulate economic growth and improve living conditions, adding that social interventions are his administration’s priorities. He said that N320 billion was proposed for the two Ministries of Works to sustain infrastructure development and complete ongoing projects In the education sector, N74 billion was proposed, comprising N10 billion for primary, N12 billion for technical, N12 billion for secondary and N40 billion for higher education. For healthcare, the proposed N50 billion allocation will support hospital upgrades, medical supplies, recruitment and welfare of health personnel. Other allocations include N50 billion for the 25 local government areas, N20 billion for the Delta State Capital Territory Development Agency and N20 billion for the Warri-Uvwie and Environs Development Agency. Read also: Bayelsa PDP slams Diri over alleged 15% 2026 budget performance The budget also provides N12 billion for energy, N10 billion for urban and physical planning, N5 billion for agriculture and N5 billion for social interventions. He restated his administration’s commitment to prudent financial management and fiscal discipline amid prevailing economic realities, promising that he would not resort to loans to fund the development agenda, just as he explained that the proposed N1.2 trillion budget was structured around the resources expected to accrue to the state. The governor clarified that the state would, however, welcome grants and other forms of financial assistance from the Federal Government, provided such support does not come with repayment obligations. “My administration will not embrace funding arrangements that require borrowing. The projects and government programmes must be implemented within the limits of available resources”, he stated. Governor Oborevwori disclosed that Delta’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) had grown from N83 billion in 2023 to a projected N283 billion by December 2026, attributing the improvement to technology-driven collection, an expanded revenue base and efforts to eliminate leakages without imposing additional tax burdens. Read also: Abandoned projects, budget rollovers slow Nigeria’s $2.3trn infrastructure ambition He further disclosed that Delta’s Gross Domestic Product rose from N14.5 trillion in 2024 to approximately N17.9 trillion in 2025, making it Nigeria’s fifth-largest state economy. The governor said the 2027 budget would prioritise infrastructure, economic diversification, human capital development, peace and security, while ensuring that ordinary Deltans benefited from economic growth. Emomotimi Guwor, Speaker of the Assembly, had lauded the governor for his administration’s achievements in infrastructure, healthcare, education, social welfare and human capital development and reaffirmed the legislature’s commitment to a cordial working relationship with the executive, noting that the House would take second reading of the bill on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.
